milestone: Cereja UI: independent toolkit and terminal application

tasks.title: Freeze Cereja UI contracts and executable evidence
tasks.risk: Model evidence can be mistaken for implemented platform support.
acceptance: Review architecture, requirement coverage, source revision, primary references and bounded spike results; distinguish supported findings, choices and unknowns.
Freeze Unicode policy, capability overrides, terminal ownership, queue limits, failure semantics and platform validation matrix before dependent implementation.
Record model baselines with raw samples, reproducible commands and measured comparison gates; record pending end-to-end budget calibration explicitly.
tasks.evidence: Contract decision record plus spike source, tests and raw baseline data. No production feature or full-platform pass is implied.
tasks.docs: docs/design/cereja-ui.md; docs/design/cereja-ui-evidence.md; benchmarks/ui_spikes/

tasks.title: Implement capabilities, virtual backend and transactional terminal sessions
tasks.risk: Partial acquisition can leak modes or contaminate redirected output.
acceptance: Implement independent input/output detection, conservative overrides, NO_COLOR and plain mode without importing legacy display.
Virtual backend injects input, clock, dimensions and output failures and exposes final cells.
Lifecycle tests cover every acquisition failure, exception, Ctrl+C, repeated cleanup and unavailable/redirected streams; plain mode writes no ESC and creates no animation timers.
tasks.evidence: unittest fault-injection matrix and capability fixtures; backend/session contract documentation.
tasks.docs: cereja.ui terminal/testing modules

tasks.title: Implement POSIX input, wakeup and terminal restoration
tasks.risk: Fragmented input or signal handling can lose keys and hang shutdown.
acceptance: Use Python 3.11-compatible termios/tty plus selectors/self-pipe, preserving captured modes and handlers.
Test fragmented UTF-8/escape/paste, Escape timeout boundaries, EOF, resize, posted wakeup and Ctrl+C.
Run PTY tests on Linux and macOS for normal/error/partial startup cleanup, and record any real-terminal gaps separately.
tasks.evidence: PTY logs with OS/Python plus parser fixtures and backend documentation.
tasks.docs: POSIX terminal backend

tasks.title: Implement Windows console records, wakeup and VT fallback
tasks.risk: Socket selector assumptions do not work for console handles; paste detection varies.
acceptance: Bind typed ctypes console/wait/event APIs, wait for input and application wake, enable VT only when supported and restore modes.
Normalize repeats/modifiers/surrogates/resize and document ambiguous paste semantics; test invalid handles and non-console fallback.
Run real Windows console restoration and input checks beyond mocked records; report terminal host/version and partial initialization cases.
tasks.evidence: Win32 record fixtures, native wait tests and real-console transcript; no universal paste claim.
tasks.docs: Windows terminal backend

tasks.title: Implement pinned grapheme metrics and safe text normalization
tasks.risk: Code-point length and East Asian Width alone corrupt clusters and alignment.
acceptance: Ship pinned Unicode segmentation/property data and license/provenance/hash/regeneration instructions with zero runtime downloads.
Use one metrics policy for layout, clipping, editing and cursor motion; cover all named ASCII/accent/CJK/emoji/ZWJ/flag/isolated-mark fixtures.
Neutralize ESC/C0/C1/DEL before measurement, define tab/newline layout and source bidi-control visibility, ambiguous widths and ASCII/unsupported-cluster fallback.
tasks.evidence: Pinned official grapheme conformance tests plus width-policy, clipping and injection fixtures; emulator differences explicitly documented.
tasks.docs: text/metrics and generated Unicode data

tasks.title: Implement cell buffers and deterministic clipped composition
tasks.risk: Wide-cell continuations and overlapping geometry leave stale pixels.
acceptance: Represent leading and continuation cells, effective styles, blank/zero-size frames and deterministic z-order.
Replacing either half of a wide glyph clears its previous footprint; clipping never leaves half a grapheme.
Fixed-seed randomized overlap/move/remove/resize tests compare complete final frames to an independent reference.
tasks.evidence: unittest golden cell grids, randomized seed logs and buffer allocation baseline at 80x24/120x40/240x80.
tasks.docs: rendering buffer/compositor

tasks.title: Implement diff, secure encoding and committed output transactions
tasks.risk: Incorrect damage or partial writes desynchronize terminal and front buffer.
acceptance: Retain full-frame diff as oracle; dirty results are equivalent for text/style/occupancy changes, resize and overlapping damage.
Unchanged frame/session emits zero writes/flushes; serialize only trusted control sequences, test last-column and bottom-right no-scroll behavior.
Commit front only after full count and flush; cover short/zero writes, flush failure, broken pipe, recovery and plain snapshot behavior.
tasks.evidence: Seeded equivalence/injection/fault tests and stage timings/bytes/write counts for unchanged, one-cell, row,10%,100% workloads.
tasks.docs: rendering diff/encoder/writer

tasks.title: Implement event scheduling, bounded posting and cancellable timers
tasks.risk: Producer pressure or polling can consume idle CPU and starve input.
acceptance: UI-thread mutation/writes only, ordered input, monotonic heap timers and backend wake for posted work/shutdown.
Idle without pending work waits indefinitely and emits no periodic redraw; late timers skip obsolete animation frames.
Test queue saturation, coalesced progress/resize, paste/sequence limits, 10,000-event fairness, widget removal, global motion disable and prompt shutdown.
tasks.evidence: Fake-clock deterministic scheduling tests plus native wake integration; measured idle counters and input fairness report.
tasks.docs: event loop and scheduling

tasks.title: Define Cereja UI v1 Product Scope
tasks.risk: Exploratory visuals or existing CLI commands can silently become unsupported product requirements.
acceptance: Record the accepted objective: discover, inspect and execute existing Cereja capabilities plus toolkit reference/dogfooding; primary Python developers/technical library and CLI users, secondary contributors/maintainers.

Record accepted five areas and file-plus-directory Compress/Decompress scope with separate safety stages. Preserve bounded explicit-path Tree and explicit-root Context Search, System and URL/destination Download; do not invent broader browser/HTTP features.

Separate established choices from hypotheses and final acceptance. Home, System, Examples, capability catalogue and Diagnostics are inline shell views anchored by the persistent bottom composer. Tree is not a full browser and Download is not a full HTTP client. Broader catalogue remains CLI/Python API references.
Record consequences for reusable toolkit coverage without blocking independent terminal/rendering core. Authorize final UX specification and product-driven decomposition only after this decision.

Preserve honest long-operation execution: use real progress/speed/ETA only; safe cooperative Cancel only where proven; otherwise indeterminate Running and actual duration/result/error. Generic domain instrumentation is separate and may be deferred with evidence without dropping the functional baseline.

Record explicit user selection of Ledger (A) and file-plus-directory v1 scope. Preserve non-selected Workbench and historical functional references. Derive flow-traceable planning tasks from the selected shell specification without authorizing production implementation.
tasks.evidence: Accepted product-scope decision with actual answers, rationale, exclusions, selected flows and open items. Existing exploratory wireframes are inputs, not acceptance.
tasks.docs: docs/design/cereja-ui-product-scope.md; exploratory visual studies

tasks.title: Specify and validate final Cereja UI UX after product scope
tasks.risk: Final screens and component requirements are invalid until the product decision is known.
acceptance: Use accepted product scope and reviewed visual language to finalize shell views, composer/slash/navigation, keyboard overlays and exact-cell layouts. Preserve existing functional wireframes as evidence; loading/empty/error/success/warning are inline states, not independent screens.
Specify visual hierarchy, reference layouts, component catalogue/states, keys/focus/selection/scroll, responsive policies, themes/colors/spacing/borders/density/accessibility/no-color/no-motion.
Evaluate every requested loading/motion/feedback effect with shared timers/dirty rendering, rate ceilings, low-bandwidth and static fallbacks.
Validate selected task walkthroughs and derive required components from those screens; record user review and limitations before high-level implementation tasks are accepted.
tasks.evidence: Final scope-traceable UX and design/motion system, wireframes and actual walkthrough evidence, distinguishing structural and user validation.
tasks.docs: Final UX artifacts to be created only after SCOPE; current visuals exploratory

tasks.title: Calibrate independent core performance against reproducible baselines
tasks.risk: Sparse synthetic timings can be mistaken for end-to-end application guarantees.
acceptance: Freeze full/sparse/resize/text/timer workloads and environment before comparing candidate optimizations; measure stage timings, bytes, calls, allocations, idle counters and fresh imports.
Use the current measured model as feasibility evidence only. Set production core comparison budgets from its actual baseline, and retain future application latency calibration as a separate gate.
Demonstrate zero unchanged output, no idle periodic redraw and bounded producer fairness. Native acceleration requires profiled failed budgets plus evaluated Python alternatives.
tasks.evidence: Raw baseline/control/treatment samples, profiles, budget rationale and scope limits; no application performance claim.
tasks.docs: Core benchmark and profiling report

tasks.title: Validate independent terminal and rendering core across supported platforms
tasks.risk: A virtual or Windows-only check can hide POSIX/macOS lifecycle and transport errors.
acceptance: Run Python3.11-3.14 core contracts on Windows/Linux/macOS, POSIX PTYs and real Windows console checks.
Record terminal hosts for resize/Unicode/restoration/no-color/ASCII/no-motion/SSH and distinguish missing hosts from passes.

Verify zero runtime dependencies, pinned Unicode notices, lazy import isolation and plain/pipes/CI/broken-pipe behavior; defer official application CLI acceptance until its scope and implementation exist.
tasks.evidence: Core CI/platform matrix, clean-install records and actual host logs with honest gaps.
tasks.docs: Core platform acceptance report

tasks.title: Decompose scope-approved widgets, application and later compatibility delivery
tasks.risk: Premature widget/application tasks bake exploratory product assumptions into implementation.
acceptance: Create small dependency-ordered tasks from the selected Ledger flows, including accepted file and directory archive modes with separate safety gates. Each task includes meaningful tests, benchmarks, documentation, risks and expected evidence; no production implementation is authorized by issue creation.
Keep toolkit reusable and independent from legacy display. Preserve required toolkit capabilities while distinguishing screen-derived widgets from independently justified reusable primitives.
Add official application integration, real-task dogfooding and end-to-end/platform/package acceptance stages; app must consume public toolkit APIs.

After new-system stabilization, schedule legacy characterization and choose adapter/wrapper/facade/controlled refactor using objective contracts; then decompose display integration/migration. Do not preselect deprecation or let legacy incompatibilities block the core.
Associate authorized follow-up issues with the Cereja UI milestone and explicit dependencies; do not execute production implementation merely because tasks exist.
tasks.evidence: Reviewed dependency DAG, small verified GitHub tasks with milestone associations and screen-to-component traceability, including explicit later legacy stage.
tasks.docs: Future implementation decomposition after accepted scope and UX

tasks.title: Implement cell layout and bounded scroll viewports
tasks.flow: All Ledger views; fixed bottom composer above resize-safe content
tasks.risk: Content and pager can overwrite the composer or lose the selected item on resize.
acceptance: Implement composable cell-based row/column constraints, padding, clipping and scroll viewports independently from the official application.
Keep composer allocation fixed at 120x40, 80x24 and 40x12; reserve a separate pager row; test nested clipping, zero/undersized dimensions and resize with a selected item.
Expose dirty regions and bounded layout invalidation; benchmark resize and long content with frozen workloads; document geometry and overflow policy.
tasks.evidence: Deterministic cell snapshots, resize/clipping tests and measured layout baseline.
tasks.docs: Selected Ledger UX and operation contracts; public API documentation and runnable bounded examples required.

tasks.title: Implement text input, focus and keyboard selection
tasks.flow: Composer editing, forms and result navigation
tasks.risk: Unicode editing or focus changes can lose input or trigger an unintended action.
acceptance: Implement grapheme-aware editing, cursor visibility, selection and paste sanitization with the accepted Unicode policy; no raw terminal controls from text.
Provide explicit focus scopes, forward/backward traversal, selection markers and focus restoration; test long input, combining/ZWJ text, narrow resize and overlay return.
Keep input bindings separate from application command parsing; publish examples and measured input-to-frame baseline.
tasks.evidence: Virtual-backend keyboard scenarios and Unicode regression cases with documented unsupported cases.
tasks.docs: Selected Ledger UX and operation contracts; public API documentation and runnable bounded examples required.

tasks.title: Implement suggestion lists, parameter forms and confirmation overlays
tasks.flow: Slash insertion, missing fields, help and exact destination confirmation
tasks.risk: Autocomplete or modal dismissal can accidentally execute or confirm stale parameters.
acceptance: Suggestion acceptance inserts and closes without execution; only a subsequent explicit submission validates or starts work. Test Enter, Tab, Escape, filtering and empty matches.
Implement generic forms with visible labels/errors and anchored overlays that fit compact terminals; help restores underlying view, draft, caret and selection.

Confirmation binds the exact normalized action/source/destination and invalidates after edits; destructive/default overwrite must never be the default selection. Document overlay focus and restoration.
tasks.evidence: Keyboard replay tests including first-Enter/second-Enter regression, compact snapshots and stale-confirmation tests.
tasks.docs: Selected Ledger UX and operation contracts; public API documentation and runnable bounded examples required.

tasks.title: Implement tables, selectable lists and hierarchical TreeView
tasks.flow: System fields, Context hits and Tree navigation
tasks.risk: Large collections can cause unbounded layout or selection drift.
acceptance: Implement read-only tables and selectable lists with stable IDs, clipping, Unicode truncation and scroll selection; do not require filesystem types.
TreeView consumes generic hierarchical nodes with expansion/loading/incomplete/error states; arrows expand/collapse/select without a full filesystem browser.
Test empty/error/disappeared nodes, broad/deep fixtures and resize preservation; benchmark visible-region work and retained node limits. Document complete versus truncated results.
tasks.evidence: Collection widget snapshots, stable-selection tests and bounded large-fixture measurements.
tasks.docs: Selected Ledger UX and operation contracts; public API documentation and runnable bounded examples required.

tasks.title: Implement reusable inline status, progress and motion components
tasks.flow: All inline loading, empty, error, success and warning states
tasks.risk: Visual motion or progress can imply nonexistent operational evidence.
acceptance: Provide labelled inline states, determinate ProgressBar only with valid measured advance/total, and indeterminate spinner/shimmer for known active work.
Use shared timers and dirty regions; provide static no-motion, low-capability and plain equivalents with text state independent of color.

Cover pulse, blink, dots, spinner, shimmer, progress and transitions in documented examples; keep typewriter/stagger/glow/fade/slide opt-in and omit them when terminal capabilities or reading stability make them unsuitable.
Test disabled motion creates no animation timer, idle views emit no redraw, completion unsubscribes timers, and reduced modes never manufacture percentages. Benchmark aggregate animation load.
tasks.evidence: Lifecycle/timer tests, capability snapshots and measured shared-animation workload.
tasks.docs: Selected Ledger UX and operation contracts; public API documentation and runnable bounded examples required.

tasks.title: Implement typed background operation lifecycle bridge
tasks.flow: One active operation while the shell stays responsive
tasks.risk: Sustained progress or blocking domain calls can starve input or imply false cancellation.
acceptance: Define UI-independent typed start/progress/result/error events, one active operation, bounded coalescing and terminal completion delivery; workers never draw.

Reject a second operation explicitly without queueing; allow navigation while work continues and preserve a bounded active-job status. Quitting an uncancellable operation offers wait/return, not a fake Cancel.
Expose Cancel only through a domain capability proving safe cooperative interruption; callback exceptions and process termination are not automatically cancellation.

Test sustained producer/input fairness against the core starvation contract, stale events, completion races, worker errors and shutdown; document lifecycle and measure input responsiveness under operation load.
tasks.evidence: Deterministic worker/event tests, producer-pressure latency evidence and documented cancellation capability boundary.
tasks.docs: Selected Ledger UX and operation contracts; public API documentation and runnable bounded examples required.

tasks.title: Build Ledger shell, slash grammar and lazy capability catalogue
tasks.flow: Home, command discovery, help, Examples and Diagnostics
tasks.risk: Discovery can eagerly initialize capabilities or turn shell syntax into arbitrary code execution.
acceptance: Build selected Ledger using public cereja.ui APIs: ordered ephemeral result blocks with selectable prior results and independent composer state. Proposed caps are 20 completed summaries and 2 MiB sanitized retained state, calibrated during implementation; evict oldest completed only, never an active operation, no disk history or retained sensitive fields. Preserve selection/scroll unless already following latest; completion never steals focus.
Register explicit commands for Home/System/Tree/Context/Compress/Download/Examples/Tools/Diagnostics/Help; parse registered commands only, never eval or OS-shell arbitrary input.
Catalogue badges distinguish actually executable UI, CLI, Python API and planned integrations. Discovery reads static metadata without eager service imports or side effects.

Implement truthful parameter/help overlays, non-executable wider catalogue and labelled synthetic examples; test keyboard-only walkthroughs, no-color/no-motion/plain and source-safe rendering. Measure startup/import side effects.
tasks.evidence: Shell keyboard snapshots, lazy import tests, catalogue truth audit, startup benchmark and user documentation.
tasks.docs: Selected Ledger UX and operation contracts; public API documentation and runnable bounded examples required.

tasks.title: Integrate System Information into Ledger
tasks.flow: System command, explicit refresh, section results and unavailable fields
tasks.risk: Hardware collection can block or expose sensitive fields.
acceptance: Use the existing typed hardware.info facade with basic/non-sensitive defaults and explicit Run/Refresh; no automatic periodic polling.
Show loading/actual elapsed duration, structured sections and unavailable/warning values without zero substitution; no Cancel or numeric progress without a proven domain capability.

Test partial/unavailable/error collectors through fixtures, refresh serialization and navigation during collection; benchmark bounded collector scenarios and document platform limitations without claiming all collectors run on one host.
tasks.evidence: Mocked integration tests, owned-host smoke where available, section snapshots and collector latency evidence.
tasks.docs: Selected Ledger UX and operation contracts; public API documentation and runnable bounded examples required.

tasks.title: Expose bounded structured repository traversal
tasks.flow: Tree root loading and lazy expand/collapse
tasks.risk: The current formatted-string API cannot safely provide TreeView hierarchy or bounded breadth.
acceptance: Extract/reuse current repository filtering/root/link rules into UI-independent typed nodes and bounded child enumeration; do not parse rendered glyphs or copy ignore logic into widgets.
Define stable IDs, ordering/pagination, depth/node/work bounds and explicit incomplete/error results, including empty directories and disappeared nodes. Links are displayed but not descended.

Test parity with existing filtering, wide/deep directories, permission failures, symlink roots and deterministic paging using owned temporary fixtures; benchmark retained memory and enumeration work. Document proposed default limits as calibrated choices.
tasks.evidence: Traversal contract tests, CLI rule parity evidence and measured broad/deep fixture bounds.
tasks.docs: Selected Ledger UX and operation contracts; public API documentation and runnable bounded examples required.

tasks.title: Integrate explicit-path hierarchical Tree into Ledger
tasks.flow: Tree parameters, hierarchy navigation and result inspection
tasks.risk: Integration can grow into a general filesystem browser or hide partial results.
acceptance: Validate explicit root/depth, load structured domain nodes into generic TreeView and preserve selected/expanded IDs across bounded child loads.
Expose loading/incomplete/error nodes and Unicode truncation with a full-value inspection affordance; no file mutation or generic browser operations.
Test keyboard expand/collapse, large volumes, path disappearance, narrow resize and navigation during work; document filters/limits and measure end-to-end visible-node response.
tasks.evidence: Owned-directory integration fixtures, keyboard flow snapshots and bounded-tree timing/memory evidence.
tasks.docs: Selected Ledger UX and operation contracts; public API documentation and runnable bounded examples required.

tasks.title: Integrate explicit-root Context Search into Ledger
tasks.flow: Query/root form, search, matches, empty/error and hit inspection
tasks.risk: Result caps can be mistaken for bounded traversal or safe cooperative cancellation.
acceptance: Use typed ContextResponse/results/snippets/skip reasons with explicit roots/query and documented filters; default cache off unless separately accepted.
Preserve safe highlighted spans, result selection, readable full-path/snippet inspection and honest incomplete/skip reporting; no automatic file opening or writes.
Execute existing API indeterminately with no Cancel; distinguish final max_results from scan/work limits and reject workloads outside documented v1 bounds rather than claiming a hard scan bound.
Test no-hit, skipped/binary/permission errors, literal control characters, long Unicode paths and selection restoration; benchmark owned search fixtures and document performance limits.
tasks.evidence: Typed adapter tests, safe-highlight snapshots and owned-fixture scan measurements.
tasks.docs: Selected Ledger UX and operation contracts; public API documentation and runnable bounded examples required.

tasks.title: Integrate safe single-file Compress and Decompress workflows
tasks.flow: Action/source/destination form, review, running and actual outcome
tasks.risk: Existing direct writes and whole-file memory use can damage output or exhaust resources.
acceptance: Use existing compression APIs with verbose=False through a typed adapter; inspect actual source/output mode and validate explicit bounds before execution.

Stage output in an owned adjacent temporary path, validate result and commit safely; exact-target overwrite confirmation must precede execution and be revalidated at commit. Never silently overwrite source or unrelated output.
Baseline is indeterminate Running with actual duration/result/error and no Cancel. Do not scrape legacy display or manufacture progress.

Test roundtrip, invalid input, source/destination collision, existing destination, commit failure and cleanup preserving previous output; measure time/peak memory on bounded fixtures and document supported limits. Directory mode is accepted v1 scope with its own safety and integration tasks; this slice covers single files.
tasks.evidence: Temporary-file integration tests, overwrite/failure recovery evidence and size/memory baseline.
tasks.docs: Selected Ledger UX and operation contracts; public API documentation and runnable bounded examples required.

tasks.title: Integrate URL download with real progress and safe destination review
tasks.flow: URL/destination review, known/unknown total transfer and outcome
tasks.risk: Unbounded network input, destination races or misleading transfer telemetry can violate the flow contract.
acceptance: Validate supported URL scheme and explicit destination; keep one active background operation, finite connection/read behavior and documented v1 byte limits; no full HTTP client interface.

Use TransferProgress bytes/optional total. Render known total only when valid; unknown total shows bytes plus indeterminate state. Derive speed/ETA only from an explicitly measured/tested sampling contract or omit them.
Reuse staging/abort semantics while enforcing exact-target overwrite authorization and bounded transfer policy; no Cancel until safe cooperative read/commit behavior is proven.

Test owned loopback known/unknown total, network/read error, misleading length, byte limit, existing target, final commit failure and partial cleanup. Document redirected URLs/destination behavior and benchmark bounded transfer responsiveness.
tasks.evidence: Loopback integration tests and preserved-target cleanup evidence, real telemetry snapshots and responsive UI benchmark.
tasks.docs: Selected Ledger UX and operation contracts; public API documentation and runnable bounded examples required.

tasks.title: Evaluate generic progress and cooperative cancellation extensions
tasks.risk: UI-only callbacks or superficial stop buttons can compromise domain reuse and safe commit.
acceptance: Assess domain-level typed progress and cooperative stop points usable by CLI/UI/external callers with no cereja.ui dependency.
For each service distinguish observable total/advance, interruptible waits, cleanup and commit boundary; include cost and failure/race evidence.

Prototype only a bounded promising seam with controls; accept instrumentation only when proportionate. Otherwise explicitly retain current functional indeterminate/no-Cancel baseline and defer richer telemetry.
Record API compatibility, test strategy and documentation impact before follow-up implementation. This investigation does not block the baseline application integrations.
tasks.evidence: Per-service proportionality decision and bounded race/cleanup experiment; no blanket cancellation claim.
tasks.docs: Selected Ledger UX and operation contracts; public API documentation and runnable bounded examples required.

tasks.title: Validate real Ledger workflows, package and platform acceptance
tasks.flow: Five real capabilities plus catalogue/examples and shell lifecycle
tasks.risk: Browser fixtures or one-host checks can be mistaken for accepted cross-platform product behavior.
acceptance: Run end-to-end owned fixtures for all five areas including file and directory archive operations, keyboard-only navigation, first/second Enter semantics, confirmation, no-color/no-motion/plain, resize and quit during active work.
Run actual-terminal Windows/Linux/macOS matrix including restoration, redirected streams and supported Python versions; missing hosts remain pending, never passed from virtual/browser evidence.

Calibrate end-to-end input/layout/paint/write latency, idle output, memory and lazy startup against frozen measured workloads; report raw reproducible evidence and proposed/accepted budgets distinctly.
Run user task walkthroughs, document discoverability/flow findings, installation/CLI packaging and public API examples; record a stable-contract decision before legacy work.
tasks.evidence: Real task walkthrough record, CI/terminal matrix, package checks and calibrated application benchmark report.
tasks.docs: Selected Ledger UX and operation contracts; public API documentation and runnable bounded examples required.

tasks.title: Characterize legacy display and select compatibility strategy after stabilization
tasks.flow: Later compatibility without constraining the independent toolkit
tasks.risk: Premature adapters or deprecation can silently change observable legacy behavior.
acceptance: After a recorded stable-contract decision, characterize console/Progress/State signatures, rendering/capture, nesting, concurrency, notebooks and lazy exports.
Compare observable contracts to the new terminal ownership/model; choose adapter/wrapper/facade or controlled refactor based on evidence, preserving reasonable public compatibility.
Create small migration issues only after that strategy is reviewed, each with regression/coexistence tests, documentation, rollback boundary and acceptance evidence; do not preselect deprecation.
tasks.evidence: Legacy characterization suite, decision matrix and reviewed conditional migration issue set.
tasks.docs: Selected Ledger UX and operation contracts; public API documentation and runnable bounded examples required.

tasks.title: Establish safe bounded directory archive operations
tasks.flow: L4 directory compression and extraction safety boundary
tasks.risk: Current directory extraction lacks containment/expansion guarantees and can expose partial writes; direct reuse is not sufficient.
acceptance: Define a UI-independent archive safety policy covering canonical destination containment, absolute/parent traversal paths, Windows drive/UNC/alternate-stream names, normalized collisions, duplicate members and file/directory conflicts. Reject unsupported member types explicitly.

Define symlink and hardlink handling, source traversal/link policy and safe destination traversal. Never follow archive-controlled links outside the owned staging root; document threat/race limitations and fail closed where guarantees cannot be met.

Enforce member-count, per-member, aggregate expanded-byte and depth budgets during decoding/extraction, not only after completion; reject malformed metadata and decompression bombs using bounded owned fixtures. Distinguish format limitations from UI policy.

Stage into an owned fresh directory, validate the full outcome before publication and refuse merging into existing destinations by default. Specify supported exact-target replacement/backup/rollback semantics or refuse replacement when safe publication is unsupported; report cleanup/partial outcomes truthfully.

Test adversarial member paths, links, collisions, budget breaches, corrupt/truncated archives and publication failures, preserving preexisting data. Benchmark bounded valid archives and peak memory. Document current-API gaps and any backward-compatible generic extension before UI integration.
tasks.evidence: Domain safety tests on owned temporary roots, explicit format/platform support matrix, bounded extraction measurements and documented publication failure semantics.
tasks.docs: Archive domain contract and public API safety documentation; no dependency on cereja.ui.

tasks.title: Integrate directory Compress and Decompress into Ledger
tasks.flow: L4 accepted file and directory modes in one Archives area
tasks.risk: A mode toggle could bypass directory safety policy or imply atomic merging into existing directories.
acceptance: Expose explicit file/directory mode under the same Compress/Decompress command flow. Validate source/destination and domain policy before execution; directory mode must not call unsafe legacy extraction directly.

Present supported limits and exact destination effects, default existing-directory refusal, and confirmation only for a supported reviewed replacement policy. No automatic merge, source deletion, symlink traversal or overwrite escalation.

Use indeterminate Running with actual result/duration and no Cancel unless a separately proven domain extension is available. Report excluded/rejected members and partial/cleanup/publication outcomes clearly without fake percentages.

Test directory roundtrips, empty trees, nested Unicode names, conflict/refusal, safety-policy rejection and staging cleanup through the actual adapter in owned temporary roots. Measure end-to-end time/memory and document supported directory/archive modes.
tasks.evidence: Owned-directory integration fixtures, safety-policy propagation and result/confirmation snapshots, measured bounded directory workload.
tasks.docs: Ledger L4 archive workflow and directory safety/limits documentation.

selected_visual_direction: Ledger (A), explicitly selected by the maintainer; planning only.
